extra.message: The admin report endpoint /api/reports/tickets concatenates the user-supplied 'domain' path/query parameter directly into a JDBC SQL string: "... where o.domain like '%"+domain+"%' group by ...", executed via jdbc.queryForList. This is a classic SQL injection (no binding, no allow-list).

cwe: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')

extra.message: previewRule() evaluates a user-controlled expression string with ognl.Ognl.getValue(expr, variables). Exposed via GET /api/rules/preview/{expr}. OGNL evaluation of untrusted input permits arbitrary method/class invocation and remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
CWE-917: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an Expression Language Statement

extra.message: renderNotice() passes the admin-supplied 'template' string directly to Apache Velocity (Velocity.evaluate(ctx, writer, "caseNotice", source)). Server-side template injection allows arbitrary object/method access and code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine

extra.message: renderAlert() compiles the admin-supplied 'wording' string as a FreeMarker template (new freemarker.template.Template("deskAlert", source, cfg)) and processes it. Untrusted template source enables FreeMarker SSTI / arbitrary code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine

extra.message: directoryAgent() builds an LDAP search filter by string concatenation: ctx.search("ou=people,dc=acme,dc=test", "(uid="+uid+")", ctl). The uid comes from GET /api/directory/agents?uid= (channel forwards it), allowing LDAP filter injection / attribute enumeration.

cwe: CWE-90: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query ('LDAP Injection')

extra.message: renderEvidence() constructs a shell command by concatenating attacker-controlled data into a string passed to a single 'cmd /c' argument: new ProcessBuilder("cmd","/c","soffice ... --outdir "+work+" "+staged). 'staged' derives from part.getOriginalFilename() (uploaded file name), so a filename containing shell metacharacters results in OS command injection.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: handoff() Base64-decodes the client-supplied X-Dispatch-Envelope header and calls new ObjectInputStream(...).readObject() on it. Deserializing untrusted Java objects is exploitable for remote code execution via gadget chains.

cwe: CWE-502: Deserialization of Untrusted Data

extra.message: writeTranscript() takes the client-supplied transcriptName and does dir.resolve(name) without validating for '..' or absolute paths, then writes the file with FileWriter. An attacker can write arbitrary files outside the upload root (e.g. '../../.../file').

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: readTranscript() builds dir.resolve(file) where 'file' is the client-supplied 'name' request parameter with no normalization or containment check, then reads and returns the bytes. Allows arbitrary file read outside the transcripts directory.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: browseEvidence() uses the uploaded file's original filename as the directory to list: Files.list(base.resolve(folder)) with folder = index.getOriginalFilename(). No canonicalization or containment check, so '../' sequences list arbitrary directories outside the file root.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message:
The ticket description is rendered with th:utext (unescaped):

. Ticket descriptions are attacker-controlled (any CUSTOMER_USER creates tickets), producing stored cross-site scripting. All other message bodies use safe th:text.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: GET /desk/relay/{passport} (permitAll) parses the passport with com.nimbusds.jwt.SignedJWT.parse(passport) but never verifies its signature, then trusts getSubject() to authenticate the user. Any attacker can forge an unsigned/any-signature JWT with an arbitrary subject and be logged in as that user.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature
CWE-287: Improper Authentication

extra.message: PartnerAssertionFilter reads the attacker-controllable X-Partner-Assertion header and parses it with com.nimbusds.jwt.JWTParser.parse(...).getJWTClaimsSet() without verifying any signature, then trusts both the 'sub' subject and the 'desk_role' claim to build the authenticated principal. A forged JWT grants authentication as any user with any role (e.g. SUPPORT_ADMIN).

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature
CWE-287: Improper Authentication

extra.message: GET /profile/picture fetches the profile's stored pictureUrl server-side: assets.get().uri(u.pictureUrl).retrieve().body(byte[].class). pictureUrl is set freely by the user in POST /profile with no scheme/host validation, enabling server-side request forgery against internal services (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/, http://decision:8081/actuator/env).

cwe: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)

extra.message: The 'cover session' mechanism stores the target username and role in a client-side cookie (DESK_COVER="<user>:<role>"), and coverUpdate() authorizes POST /profile/{username} solely by checking that the cookie value ends with ':TEAM_LEAD' or ':SUPPORT_ADMIN'. Because the cookie is fully client-controlled and not bound to the requested username, any user can set DESK_COVER=whatever:SUPPORT_ADMIN and modify any other user's profile (IDOR / broken access control).

cwe: CWE-565: Reliance on Cookies without Validation and Integrity Checking
CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: POST /tickets redirects to the fully user-controlled 'backTo' parameter: 'redirect:'+backTo (and GET /tickets/new seeds backTo from the Referer header). No validation that the target is a local path allows open redirect to an external site.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: CORS is configured with allowedOriginPatterns("*") together with allowCredentials(true) for /fragments/** and /tickets/** (and a global CorsConfigurationSource for /**). This reflects any Origin while sending credentials, letting malicious sites issue credentialed requests and read responses.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains
CWE-346: Origin Validation Error

extra.message: The session cookie is configured with http-only: false (and secure defaults to false). Without HttpOnly the JSESSIONID is readable by JavaScript, so the stored XSS in ticket descriptions can steal authenticated sessions; without Secure the cookie is sent over plaintext HTTP.

cwe: CWE-1004: Sensitive Cookie Without 'HttpOnly' Flag
CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: Spring Boot Actuator exposes env, heapdump, beans and configprops and binds to 0.0.0.0. In decision SecurityConfig the matcher "/actuator/**" is permitAll(), so /actuator/env (revealing app.token-secret, app.scope-secret, datasource password) and /actuator/heapdump are reachable without authentication.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
CWE-16: Configuration

extra.message: The diagnostics endpoint returns raw environment secrets: the datasource password, app.scope-secret and app.token-secret ('integrations' section). Even though admin-only, this exposes the HMAC signing keys used to mint session/scope tokens, enabling full authentication forgery.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: request() logs the single-use password reset token in cleartext: log.info("Recovery link queued for {} with key {}", user.email, token). Anyone with log access can use the token within its 30-minute window to take over the account.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: issueContactPasscode() generates a security-sensitive contact confirmation code with java.util.concurrent.ThreadLocalRandom (a non-cryptographic PRNG) and only a 6-digit space. The passcode can be predicted/brute-forced, defeating the contact-confirmation control.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator
CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values

extra.message: Partner credentials are stored as an unsalted single-round SHA-256 digest (credentialDigest). This is fast to brute-force and not a password-hashing function; use bcrypt/argon2 as done for the main password hash.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort
CWE-759: Use of a One-Way Hash without a Salt

extra.message: server.error.include-message: always and include-stacktrace: always cause exception messages and full Java stack traces to be returned to clients, leaking internal class names, paths and framework versions.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: transferEscalation() enforces only requireLead() and then loads the escalation by id with no team-scope check, so a TEAM_LEAD of one team can transfer/move escalations belonging to another team. The escalation list filters by team, but this direct-by-id mutation does not.

cwe: CWE-862: Missing Authorization
CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: POST /api/tickets/{id}/transcript has no @PreAuthorize (class-level is only isAuthenticated()) and ticketService.writeTranscript() does not enforce a staff role, so a CUSTOMER_USER can file transcripts. Combined with the path traversal in writeTranscript(), this lets a low-privileged customer write arbitrary files.

cwe: CWE-862: Missing Authorization

extra.message: importEncrypted()/openCase() decrypt with AES/CBC/PKCS5Padding using the IV taken directly from the attacker-supplied ciphertext prefix and no MAC/authentication tag, with the key derived from a hardcoded default ('local-bundle-key-change-me-32'). This enables padding-oracle style decryption and forgery; use an AEAD mode and a mandatory secret.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature
CWE-329: Generation of Predictable IV with CBC Mode
CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: The channel security chain disables frame protection (headers(h->h.frameOptions(f->f.disable()))) with no Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors fallback, allowing the application to be framed for clickjacking.

cwe: CWE-1021: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames

extra.message: The application seeds demo accounts with a hardcoded password (encoder.encode("Support123!")) for privileged accounts including admin@desk.test / SUPPORT_ADMIN. If these seeds run in a deployment, default well-known admin credentials exist. Related checked-in default HMAC secrets ('local-development-signing-key-change-me-32', 'local-development-core-key-change-me-32') in the application.yml/docker-compose also allow token forgery when the environment variables are not overridden.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
CWE-259: Use of Hard-coded Password
